files.title: File:Brown's Creek Tributary Masonry Arch Bridge Mitchell Co KS date stone on north rail.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption: This bridge was constructed by laborers working under the WPA program. It was constructed in 1936, as documented by a date stone in the bridge rail.
files.category: Category:Brown's Creek Tributary Masonry Arch Bridge

files.title: File:Brown's Creek Tributary Masonry Arch Bridge Mitchell Co KS southwest side.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption: The stones feature two different finishes, rusticated and smooth. They are laid in an ashlar pattern. There is a single course of smooth faced stones that corresponds to the level of the driving surface and spans the length of the bridge. The arch stones are smooth faced and each has a keystone.
files.category: Category:Brown's Creek Tributary Masonry Arch Bridge

files.title: File:Brown's Creek Tributary Masonry Arch Bridge Mitchell Co KS view from road.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption: The walls extend three courses above the driving surface, serving as bridge rails.
files.category: Category:Brown's Creek Tributary Masonry Arch Bridge

files.title: File:Brown's Creek Tributary Masonry Arch Bridge Mitchell Co KS wing wall.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption: As was typical of the era, the wings are at a 45° angle to the bridge and stair-step down from the top of the rail.
files.category: Category:Brown's Creek Tributary Masonry Arch Bridge

files.title: File:Brown's Creek Tributary Masonry Arch Bridge Mitchell Co KS.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption: The Brown’s Creek Tributary Bridge is a three-span stone arch bridge. Each span is twelve feet in length. All stones are uniform in thickness, which is approximately 8”. They vary in color from tan to gold and most have noticeable striping.
files.category: Category:Brown's Creek Tributary Masonry Arch Bridge
